title: SparseBitMatrix Cuthill-McKee row reorder
description:
Add a Cuthill-McKee row/column permutation to `SparseBitMatrix`. One-shot pre-processing that minimises matrix bandwidth, amortising cache-reuse gains across many matvecs.

## Background

LDPC parity-check matrices in `gf2-coding` have irregular row spans that hurt cache reuse during repeated matvecs. No bandwidth-minimization preprocessing currently exists.

The fix is V7 layout-only: implement Cuthill-McKee (or reverse Cuthill-McKee, RCM) row/column permutation. Apply once before dispatch; amortises across many matvecs.

API: `SparseBitMatrix::reorder_rcm() -> (SparseBitMatrix, RowPermutation)` so callers can recover the original row order on output.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Reordered + permuted result is bit-exact to original CSR matvec.
- [hard] Permutation roundtrip (apply then unapply) is identity for arbitrary input.
- [hard] Bench measures **amortised** matvec cost over $\geq 100$ calls (single-call cost is dominated by the reorder itself).
- [hard] `perf stat -r 10` capture before/after recorded for the amortised case.
- [aspirational] $\geq 1.5\times$ amortised geomean on LDPC parity-check matrix sizes.

## Notes

Bench: `sparse` (existing, pinned by I1) extended with an amortised-matvec measurement. Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
